name: xTool D1 Pro 10W
tagline: 10W engraving-focused module on the D1 Pro open-frame rail
tldr: The 10W D1 Pro module balances detail engraving and light cuts on xTool's open-frame rail. Good for gifts and leather; compare 20W or 40W modules if plywood cutting dominates your week.

priceRange.note: 10W optical module : verify SKU before buying

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

cannot: Clear acrylic cutting (diode light passes through)

pros: Engraving-focused D1 Pro module with a tighter spot than 20W/40W heads
Large 430 × 390 mm bed for coasters, signs, and batch gifts
Swappable head : upgrade to 20W or 40W later on the same rail
xTool Creative Space keeps onboarding simple before LightBurn
Strong value if you mostly mark and only cut thin basswood
cons: This module targets thin cuts (about 5 mm basswood class) : not thick production plywood
Higher modules in this line (20W or 40W) add cut speed and depth
Not the SKU for a shop cutting 5 mm+ stock all day
Open frame: kids, pets, and smoke are not contained
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 10W module on xTool D1 Pro. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other modules via the chips before buying.
proTips: Run material test grids at engraving speeds first. Add air assist for light cuts. If cut jobs exceed ~30% of your week, open the higher-watt profile on this site and compare times.
mainObjective: High-quality hobby and light-business engraving with light, slow cutting

images.alt: xTool D1 Pro 10W laser engraver : xTool

moduleSystem.headline: Swappable diode modules on D1 Pro frame
moduleSystem.description: xTool D1 Pro uses plug-in diode modules (5W–40W depending on era and listing). Buy the module power you need : same rail and software as other D1 Pro heads.

editorialDepth.advantages: The 10W D1 Pro module sits between 5W detail work and 20W mixed production : enough cut depth for typical hobby boxes while keeping engraving quality high at sensible speeds. Same rail, software, and upgrade path as heavier SKUs.
editorialDepth.limitations: Open-frame safety and ventilation are your responsibility. Thick hardwood, fast sign cutting, and clear acrylic production push you toward the 20W or 40W head or a CO₂ machine. Verify optical power on the listing : do not assume combined-watt marketing.
